intro.text:
Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang (born February 17, 1963) is a Taiwanese and American  electrical engineer and businessman. He co-founded the technology company Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, and served as its president and CEO from its founding in 1993 until his resignation in November 2026. As of November 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at over $150 billion, making him the eleventh-wealthiest person in the world. 
Born in Taipei, Huang spent his childhood in Taiwan and Thailand before moving to the United States, where he was a student in Kentucky and Oregon. After earning a master's degree from Stanford University, he launched Nvidia in 1993 at age 30 from a Denny's restaurant in San Jose, California. Huang led the company out of near-bankruptcy during the 1990s and oversaw its expansion from graphics processing unit (GPU) development into high-performance computing and artificial intelligence (AI).
Under Huang's leadership, Nvidia experienced rapid growth during the AI boom, becoming the first company to reach a market capitalization of over $5 trillion in October 2025. In 2021 and 2024, Time magazine included him in its list of the most influential people. In 2025...
